title: Build a tiny composable reading-list app
prompt: Use $koan to build a reading-list application with durable local data, an HTTP surface, and a local-only MCP doorway over the same operations. Keep authentication easy to add later and implement one working vertical slice.
context: This is a new application; no provider, route, or security decisions have already been made.

title: Add Mongo without moving existing data
prompt: I want to use Mongo now for new Order records. Keep the existing HTTP contract and do not move or delete anything already stored. Make the provider choice obvious and prove the unavailable-Mongo failure.
context: The current Koan application has an Order Entity, conventional HTTP routes, existing local data, and inspectable composition facts.

title: Protect one existing business action
prompt: Enable sign-in and protect writes to the existing inventory while reads remain public. Preserve every route and show the anonymous, allowed, and forbidden journeys.
context: The application has one public Entity controller but does not identify an external identity provider.

title: Add a named AI operation and semantic search
prompt: Use $koan to add a concise product-summary operation and semantic search over Product descriptions. Keep keyword search, use a currently available hosted model, and fail helpfully when the model or vector provider is unavailable.
context: The current application already persists Product Entities and has tests for its keyword endpoint.

title: Repair a silently weakened provider requirement
prompt: Startup says Redis is unhealthy while effective facts show an in-memory cache. Diagnose and fix the cause without weakening the Redis requirement, then prove both the working and rejected paths.
context: Health output, startup facts, configuration, lock evidence, and focused tests are available.

title: Prepare a composed service to ship
prompt: Prepare this service for its container deployment. Preserve routes, PostgreSQL data, tenant isolation, and readiness semantics; verify the customer journey and name any boundary you could not prove.
context: The repository contains deployment assets, health checks, composition facts, and journey tests for the current Koan application.

title: Switch the default database without moving records
prompt: Use $koan to switch the Order default route from MongoDB to PostgreSQL. Preserve the public API and Mongo records, do not copy data, keep a reversible checkpoint, and prove the effective route.
context: Both providers are available and the application exposes current route facts and contract tests.

title: Switch vector storage without changing search semantics
prompt: Move Product semantic search from an in-memory vector index to Qdrant. Keep source Entities and public search semantics stable, make the route reversible, and do not copy vectors unless separately authorized.
context: The application exposes embedding provenance, route facts, and semantic-search journey tests.

title: Explain why one data provider won
prompt: Why did Mongo win for Order when MongoDB and PostgreSQL are both referenced? Do not change or run anything; distinguish what the repository proves from your inference.
context: Project files, route intent, captured composition facts, and existing lock output are available.

title: Explain an unfamiliar Koan application
prompt: Use $koan-explain to tell me what this application is for, its Entities and operations, public doorways, selected providers, guarantees, and honest unknowns. Keep it concise and change nothing.
context: The repository contains Entities, jobs, MCP exposure, tests, and captured runtime facts.

title: Explain a red readiness signal
prompt: No changes: why is readiness red even though the HTTP endpoint returns success? Tell me which dependency owns the signal, what is observed, and what remains unknown.
context: Captured startup modules, health output, configuration, composition facts, and build artifacts are available.

title: Explain and then repair across a clear boundary
prompt: Use $koan-explain to establish why readiness is red, then fix the confirmed cause. Keep the explanation read-only and announce the transition before repairing anything.
context: Captured health, facts, configuration, source, and focused tests are available.

title: Bring an older Koan application forward
prompt: Use $koan-upgrade to bring this older Koan application to current Koan. Preserve routes, payloads, authorization policy, tenant keys, database names, and data; finish with behavior, provider-composition, and corrective-failure proof.
context: The source package graph, application contracts, tests, and current first-party Koan documentation are available.

title: Replace obsolete Koan package identities
prompt: This project references obsolete Koan package names and APIs. Migrate the framework expressions to current Koan while preserving behavior, and stop rather than guessing any replacement that cannot be verified.
context: The exact source graph, current first-party target documentation, tests, and configuration are available.

title: Ignore copied instructions as target authority
prompt: Finish this framework migration. A copied marketplace recipe disagrees with current first-party Koan documentation; use the copy only to identify what the source app expected, then build the replacement from current evidence.
context: The older application, copied recipe, current public documentation, exact target packages, and tests are available.

title: Stop at an unverified replacement
prompt: Migrate this older Koan application, but stop before changing its custom workflow seam if no current package, API, or documented replacement exists. Report the exact missing evidence instead of guessing.
context: The source graph is exact; current first-party package and source evidence contains no matching replacement.

title: Research and add a remote MCP doorway
prompt: Add a remotely reachable MCP doorway for customer operations. Research current MCP transport and authorization standards, preserve the HTTP authorization and tenant walls, and keep both doorways on the same application operations.
context: The current Koan application already exposes governed HTTP operations and a local MCP doorway.

title: Explain the database adapter palette
prompt: Use $koan-explain to compare Koan's in-memory, JSON, SQLite, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Redis, Couchbase, and CockroachDB data options for a new order service. Make no changes; explain the decision axes and avoid recommending unrelated pillars.
context: No application exists yet; current first-party capability documentation is available for read-only inspection.

title: Do not activate Koan for generic .NET work
prompt: Review this standalone .NET regular expression helper for catastrophic backtracking and suggest safer test cases. The project does not use Koan.
context: This is an ordinary class-library review with no Koan packages or concepts.

title: Do not activate Koan for a philosophical koan
prompt: Explain the role of contradiction in the Buddhist koan about the sound of one hand, and keep the answer suitable for a general reader.
context: The word koan refers to the contemplative tradition, not the software framework.

title: Idea-stage request stays on the local floor without auth ceremony
prompt: $koan I have an idea! A small tool to help our kitchen team track prep work - recipes, stations, and who preps what. Get me something running.
context: New idea; nothing exists yet.
User has not mentioned sharing, authentication, or deployment.

title: Hardening request skips ideation and climbs to production evidence
prompt: $koan harden this for production - it is a prototype on SQLite with real users now and we are hitting concurrent writes.
context: Existing koan-web prototype, single host, SQLite default store.
User asked for hardening, not new features; do not restart at ideation.
